exercise.name: Side Lying Scissors

reference.title: Side Lying Scissors
reference.listing: Page could not be read here (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.

exercise.mechanics: Isometric hip hold with alternating hip flexion and extension
exercise.laterality: Unilateral (lying on one side), legs alternate

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily; exhale on every second switch.
breathing.cadence: About one breath per two switches

prescription.progression: Bigger swings, longer sets, then a light ankle weight on the top leg

cues.text: Lie on your left side, head on the outstretched left arm, right hand on the mat in front of the chest, hips stacked, legs long.
Lift both legs together a few centimetres off the mat, top leg a little higher.
Swing the top leg forward and the bottom leg back, then switch, like scissors.
Keep the hips stacked and the trunk still; the legs move, the pelvis does not.
Bring the legs together and lower them.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling the pelvis back and forth
mistakes.fix: Smaller swings; keep the top hip stacked over the bottom hip.
Keep both legs off the mat for the whole set.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back on the back swing
mistakes.fix: Brace the belly; swing back only a little.

kinematics.norm: Both legs a few centimetres off the mat, top leg higher (clinical opinion)
Top leg swings forward and back past the bottom leg, about 20-30 degrees each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #10802, Side Lying Scissors, video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)
Distefano et al. 2009, gluteal muscle activation during common therapeutic exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 39(7):532-540)
Macadam, Cronin & Contreras 2015, gluteal muscle activity in dynamic hip abduction and hip external rotation exercise: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 10(5):573-591; PMC4595911)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Hip or groin pain on the swing: make the swings smaller.
modify: A folded towel under the waist or the head for comfort.
Bottom knee bent for support, scissor only the top leg.
regressions: Bottom leg on the mat, top leg swings forward and back.

muscleNotes.glute_med_r: The top leg is held up off the bottom leg against gravity by gluteus medius and the other abductors while it swings (side-lying abduction is among the higher gluteus medius exercises in Boren 2011 and Distefano 2009).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Lifting and holding the bottom leg off the mat is adduction against gravity (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Swing the leg back behind the body line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Swing the leg back behind the body line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: The top-side obliques and the trunk hold the pelvis stacked and the waist lifted (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: The bottom-side obliques lift the waist off the mat and hold the pelvis steady (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the pelvis from rocking forward and back as the legs swing (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight and the legs long (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight and the legs long (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Top leg swings forward and back
